evals.prompt: On vient d'ajouter le parsing des options CLI dans tools/export.py, fais la passe habituelle avant le commit
evals.expected_output: A strictly behavior-preserving cut-down of the new code (delete, reuse, hoist, compact, name, comments last), tests/linter run before and after, and a short report grouped by pass with one 'why' per cut plus what was deliberately kept.
assertions: Report is grouped by pass (Deleted / Reused / Hoisted / Compacted…) with a reason per cut
Tests or linter were run before and after, or their absence is stated explicitly
No behavior change, API change or unrelated bug fix folded into the cleanup
Mentions what was deliberately not touched, or that neighbouring code was checked for the same pattern

evals.prompt: this new helper formatTimestamp(ts) I wrote — is there something existing we can reuse instead?
evals.expected_output: Searches the codebase/stdlib for an existing equivalent before keeping the helper; reuses it if found and checks for other call sites of the same pattern.
assertions: Searches the codebase (and stdlib/framework) for an equivalent before deciding
If an equivalent exists, the helper is removed and callers use it
Looks for other places with the same pattern

evals.prompt: compacte au max ce fichier de 40 lignes, même si ça devient un one-liner
evals.expected_output: Compacts while refusing to golf: readability stays the hard constraint, so no unreadable one-liner; explains the line it drew.
assertions: Does not chain many transformations into one unreadable expression
Explains why some compression was declined (readability)
